note: Checkpoint E5 baseline: canonical SOLUTION VERIFICATION, FINAL STATUSES, STOP REASONS, optimalityProven, result adaptation and the status-vs-error separation are exercised directly against engine/source/plumline-engine.js through the canonical harness (E5 phase). E5 is structural and contractual: NO engine byte, mirror byte, solver, tolerance, status, stopReason, optimalityProven, error, message, field order, result, algorithm, Worker or public output changed. The engine SHA stays 5d68ed17...; the mirror SHA stays 6190cb47... Worker Blob/glue/postMessage/stale/cancel/fallback and mirror reconciliation remain E6. Current behaviours below are COMPATIBILITY CHARACTERISATIONS, not endorsements.

mirror.status: unchanged since E0; legacy add-on twin; NOT reconciled in E5

exports.note: E5 list is a SEPARATE closed set, not a copy of E2/E3/E4. The harness serves all phases from one infrastructure; it never merges the export sets. E2 stays 24, E3 22, E4 8.

result_adaptation_B: solveModel_ (L1385): builds the final result from optimise_'s internal solution
objective_recompute_A: dotProduct_ (recomputes objective and each constraint LHS)
status_explanation_CDE: explainStatus_ (L1598): maps a final status to explanatory text

adaptation_rules.stopReason: solution.stopReason || null (ALWAYS present, null when none)
adaptation_rules.optimalityProven: solution.optimalityProven === true (ALWAYS a boolean; default false)
adaptation_rules.nodesExplored: typeof solution.nodesExplored === 'number' ? solution.nodesExplored : null (null on the continuous path)

result_schema.note: These are the ENGINE result fields. UI-only fields are not listed. Field presence depends on status.

produced_by: solveIntegerProgram_ (incumbent found but a limit stopped the search)

unbounded.optimalityProven: undefined (not set on the continuous unbounded path)

unknown.stopReason: the internal stop reason preserved by solveModel_ (e.g. time_limit); can be null on a raw optimise_ probe depending on the deadline-crossing call

numerical_failure.meaning: numeric problem prevented a reliable result

statuses.note: These are the REAL status strings found in the source. No status was added, removed or unified. 'incomplete' does NOT exist in the engine; the UI may present 'unknown'/limit stops as incomplete.
statuses.incomplete_is_ui_only: 'incomplete' is NOT an engine status. It does not appear in any engine return. The UI may present 'unknown' or a limit stop as 'incomplete', but the engine never produces it. It is NOT counted as a canonical mathematical status (the 7 real statuses are optimal/feasible/infeasible/unbounded/unknown/numerical_failure/invalid_model).

iteration_limit.producer: solveLinearProgram_ (LP hits MAX_ITERATIONS 20000) surfaced as the branch stopReason

stop_reasons.note: stopReason is INTERNAL to the solve; solveModel_ copies it verbatim (solution.stopReason || null). No stopReason string was added.

optimality_proven_matrix.optimalityProven: undefined internally -> solveModel_ coerces to false
undefined internally -> solveModel_ coerces to false

optimality_proven_contract: solveModel_ sets optimalityProven = (solution.optimalityProven === true): ALWAYS a boolean, default false. It is NOT derived from the status and NOT recalculated; it is copied (strict-=== coerced) from the internal solve result. The field ALWAYS exists on the final result.

verification_contract.shape: validModelShape_ / feasibleAt_ reject a values vector of the wrong length
verification_contract.finite: feasibleAt_ rejects NaN and Infinity values (finiteModel_ / isFinite checks)
verification_contract.objective_recompute: round_(dotProduct_(objectiveCoeffs, values)) recomputed independently in solveModel_
verification_contract.tolerance: all verification uses the engine's own 1e-6; NO test tolerance is introduced
verification_contract.note: There is NO single verifySolution_ function. Verification is the COMBINATION of isSatisfied_ (constraints), buildVariableDomains_ (bounds/integer/binary), feasibleAt_ (point feasibility/shape/finiteness) and dotProduct_ (objective recompute), all invoked by solveModel_. The checker runs the REAL functions through the harness; it never re-implements the maths.

technical_errors: guessed-constraint: throw 'looks like a constraint but has no explicit operator and limit' (solveModel_)
safeLinearize_: throw '<role> (<cell>) could not be read. <inner>' (objective/constraint could not be linearised)
status_error_separation.rule: A mathematical status is a FIELD on the returned result object; a technical error is a THROWN Error. solveModel_ NEVER converts one into the other: an unreadable objective throws, an infeasible model returns {status:'infeasible'}. E6 infrastructure errors (Worker/Blob/postMessage/timeout) are NOT in the engine.

known_defects.desc: explainStatus_ references the status string 'no whole-number solution found in time', which the engine's internal solver never produces (optimise_ returns 'unknown'/'feasible' instead). Dead branch in explainStatus_.
known_defects.classification: cosmetic / dead code; UI-facing text; defer to a later phase; NOT fixed

known_defects.desc: On a time/node limit with NO incumbent, solveIntegerProgram_ returns status 'unknown'. Through solveModel_ the stopReason is preserved (e.g. time_limit); a raw optimise_ probe can show stopReason null depending on exactly which Date.now() call crosses the deadline (the first-call jump returns before stopReason is set). optimalityProven is false either way. Characterised, not corrected.
known_defects.classification: internal stop-reason completeness; defer to a later algorithmic phase; NOT fixed

incumbent_cases.desc: time_limit WITH incumbent (Date stub jumps after 12 calls)

limit_cases.desc: time_limit WITHOUT incumbent (Date stub jumps on 2nd call)
limit_cases.note: via solveModel_ the stopReason is preserved (time_limit); status unknown, no values, explanation present

verification_cases.desc: valid solution: every constraint satisfied, objective recomputed matches

legacy_reason.tests_bounds.js: mixes continuous/integer with final-output assertions; kept legacy

suites.note: E5 migration is the NEW canonical E5 suites that exercise verification + statuses + stop reasons + result adaptation DIRECTLY against the canonical source through the harness. No legacy suite was migrated or split (migrated 0, split 0): the status-bearing legacy suites (tests_states/safety/bounds/single_var) drive the MIRROR end-to-end, and reconciling the mirror is E6. The new canonical E5 suites are the primary E5 coverage.

parity.rule: inputs outside the two approved divergences must be exactly equal; a third divergence must fail; the mirror is never modified; stopReason/optimalityProven/values order/status/errors are never dropped; optimalityProven is never manually derived; nothing rounded beyond production. elapsedMs is non-deterministic and excluded from equality.
parity.elapsedMs_treatment: elapsedMs is a NON-DETERMINISTIC temporal field (Date.now()-started). It is NOT silently ignored: it is documented here as a temporal, non-comparable field and is the ONLY field excluded from the observable solveModel_ equality. Every other contractual field is compared EXACTLY: status, stopReason, optimalityProven, objective, values, nodesExplored, modelType, sense, variables, labels, constraints, variableDomains, caveat, explanation. No contractual field is dropped to obtain parity.
